sentences.text: Turiasaurus possessed a skull measuring 70 centimetres in length, a dimension paleontologists view as relatively small for an animal of its massive scale.
One of its leg bones, the femur, measured approximately 2.2 meters in length.

Early calculations based on a 1.79-meter humerus suggested the creature reached 36 to 38 meters long and weighed between 39.9 and 47.36 tonnes, while newer estimates propose a length of 21 to 30 meters and a weight between 30 and 50 tonnes.
This animal is considered the largest dinosaur ever discovered in Europe and ranks among the largest dinosaurs known globally.
The first remains were discovered on May 23, 2003, at El Húmero, just one kilometer from the town of Riodeva in the province of Teruel, Spain.

Royo-Torres, Cobos, and Alcalá formally described the type species Turiasaurus riodevensis in 2006, naming the genus after the Turia River and the Greek word for lizard, while the species name refers to the locality of Riodeva.
The skull of Turiasaurus was formally described in 2012.
Paleontologist Luis Alcalá hypothesized that Turiasaurus had a relatively small head because a larger one might have caused the animal to break its neck.
Fossils found in nearby deposits of similar age include a diplodocid sauropod, a stegosaurian, an unclassified ornithopod, crocodiles, turtles, and fish.
Phylogenetic analysis places Turiasaurus outside the Neosauropoda division within a new clade called Turiasauria, alongside Losillasaurus and Galvesaurus.
Turiasaurus is the first giant sauropod identified in the Turiasauria clade, whereas other large sauropods like Diplodocus, Brachiosaurus, and Argentinosaurus belong to the Neosauropoda clade.
Turiasaurus riodevensis lived during the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic and is known from fossils found in the Villar del Arzobispo Formation of Teruel, Spain.
Turiasaurus lived during the Late Jurassic, approximately 155 to 146 million years ago, spanning from the Kimmeridgian to the Tithonian stages in what is now Europe.
Approximately 150 million years ago, the environment where Turiasaurus lived was an extensive tidal plain cut by large rivers flowing into the Tethys Sea.
